newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close limit up, hogs up sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close limit up, hogs up sharply.

text.p: CME pork belly futures finished mostly up the daily 2.000-cent-a-lb limit on strong technical and fundamental demand while hog futures closed sharply higher in nearbys on indications of firmer cash hog markets and technical factors, traders said.
All but July pork bellies ended up the 2.000 limit with that month up 1.625 cents. February settled at 78.550 cents.

Bellies started higher on carryover technical demand and ran up the limit by late morning as added buying sparked by reports of rising cash touched off buy stops. Demand for bacon is improving, traders said.
"We had a late tomato crop" which will now boost bacon demand for bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwiches (BLTs), said Bill Cipolla, belly trader for Iowa Grain.

Lack of BLT business had accounted for part of the reduced retail demand in August. Remaining August deliveries were also sold at low prices. But now those deliveries are out of the market and cash prices are firming, Cipolla added.
USDA reported cash belly prices rose to $70 per cwt, highest levels since September 3, and there were reports of cash trading as high as $72, traders said.
Bellies looked technically strong after a reversal posted Tuesday when prices started sharply lower and finished sharply higher, they added.

Hog futures followed bellies on spillover demand with reports of active pork product sales and firmer cash hog indications for the remainder of the week also turning prices up from initial losses. Futures started lower along with live markets but packer interest for hogs improved during the morning which lifted futures into buy stops, traders said.
Technicals also appeared strong in hog futures after they held technical points Tuesday, they said.
Early indications on next week's Hogs and Pigs report point to continued lower-than-year-ago hog supplies. Indications for increased farrowings limited gains in deferred summer contracts, they added.

R.J. O'Brien, Merrill Lynch and FIMAT Futures USA were notable buyers in October, traders said. Cargill Investor Services sold on the scale-up. In hog options, locals bought October 54 to 58 calls on the rally, sources said.
Hog futures closed 0.900 cent a lb higher to unchanged with October up most at 55.525 cents per lb.
